chapter_title: There is no Joy that shall remain in the World til

6.content: and fetter it in the lump

spiritual_reading:
No one in the natural degree remains in a stable conjunction of good and truth such that full blessedness can endure without interruption to the completion of the process.

Not only those who are in the external form of human life, but even those universal governing powers that give understanding and affection their illumination and warmth, are maintained in their appointed order without being forced, because they do not act from rebellion against what rules them. Yet even these cannot be in unbroken fullness of delight while disorder still stands opposed within the created domain.

First, the mind’s discernment is turned toward the reigning evil, and it perceives it clearly in its repulsive forms. It sees that this evil is active and confirmed, and that it exercises dominion in inner things and outer things, secretly and openly, doing whatever it desires from its own love.

Second, the same discernment perceives the living spiritual principle within people, and sees that it is caught and bound by a great constraint in inner and outer levels, held within perverted perception and within corrupt life, under continual compulsion. It is pressed, drawn into proximity, divided against itself, and made subservient whenever it rises toward higher things or descends into lower things; it is driven in alternation from higher to lower states and from lower to higher states, and is stripped and transferred from one external form to another.

Because that living spiritual principle is loved and held in reverence, when it is seen under such oppression, the powers that love it cannot be in complete joy.

Thus there is grief for the living spiritual principle, and grief for the ruling evil that is seen governing what is not its own. That evil exults and is satisfied with appropriated good and truth that do not belong to it. For this reason there is not yet total rejoicing; yet there is endurance and inward restraint until the living spiritual principle is purified and taken out of the dominion of evil. Then the intention of spiritual death, which is the enemy, is removed from operation and confined so that it can no longer go forth into life.

When, at the completion, the ruling evil is finally bound so that it cannot act, then joy becomes full and grief ceases from that point. Then the state is restored in permanence to what it was in its first purity, to eternity.

fills.notes: The substrate point is universal: no embodied subject in the created order (the mixed domain) has unbroken joy while mixture persists. The phrase marks being-in-the-world as being in the mixed state, not a moral condition.

The light-givers function as ordered governors; the oldest-layer register tends to describe them as ‘set’ or ‘appointed’ in a fixed course, not as morally struggling. This matches the spiritual sense: maintained in appointed order without oppression.
The contrast is: they are not oppressed, and they do not ‘know’ how to resist being fixed in their assigned ordinance. The surviving final ‘s’ fits the infinitival construction (‘to be set’).
Completes ‘will’. The enemy acts from its own love as will.

After ‘in the tree and in the flesh’ the substrate typically adds a binding term to restate the constraint across inner and outer forms. This supports the spiritual sense of continual compulsion across levels.

fills.fill: and shut it up in the lump
fills.notes: Adjusted from the editor’s ‘fetter’ to ‘shut up’: the spiritual sense here is not merely binding but confinement so it can no longer go forth into operation. ‘Lump’ (the final compact mass) is retained as the oldest-layer cosmological image of the inert aggregate at the end.

assessment: Most gaps are either single-letter or already tightly constrained by the chapter’s twofold structure (grief for the bound soul; grief for the reigning enemy). The only freer restorations are in ¶2 and ¶4 where the cosmological-register phrasing must express appointed order and constraint; and ¶6 where the end-state requires not just binding but final confinement of Death’s impulse into the inert ‘lump'.
